newsitem.title: USA: Alaska lawmakers override billboard veto.
newsitem.headline: Alaska lawmakers override billboard veto.

text.p: Overriding a governor's veto, the Alaska legislature loosened one of the nation's strictest prohibitions against billboards by allowing advertising on private property.

The 43-16 vote fell largely along partisan lines, with Republicans voting to overturn the actions of Democratic Gov. Tony Knowles. He opposed the bill as the first step toward a proliferation of billboards along the state's roads.
The signs are to be no more than 18 inches high and 90 inches wide.
Enforcement is to be handled by the state Department of Transportation.
Sponsor Lyda Green, a Republican state senator from Wasilla, said the legislation will help small businesses attract tourists.
